plans.note: Yearly billing: $416/mo ($4,990/yr, save $998). 10 seats (+$49/seat), 20 agents, SSO & SAML, 90-day audit log.

plans.name: Team (hosted models)
plans.note: Same as Team BYOK plus hosted OpenAI/Anthropic/Google models under fair-use limits. Yearly $416/mo ($4,990/yr). 5 fixed seats, 10 agents.

plans.name: Scale (hosted models)
plans.note: Scale plus hosted models. Yearly $1,666/mo ($19,990/yr). 10 seats included, extra seat $199/mo, 20 agents.

caveats: Free 3 seats/3 agents/500 calls and $5 AI credit; Team displayed $149 for 5 seats/10 agents with BYO key, Scale $499/10 seats/20 agents and $49 extra user. Model toggle changes totals; values not unconditional all-model subscription. VM shape and runtime caps unknown.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Hosted-model plans have fair-use token limits per session and per week. When a window is exhausted, requests go to a lightweight model until it resets (a soft cap, not overage billing). There is no metering or overage on integration calls.

Hosted micro-VM size (vCPU/RAM/disk) is not published. The self-hosted runner defaults are 1 vCPU share, 2 GiB RAM, 512 pids and 4 sandboxes per host (RUNNER_SANDBOX_CPUS=1, RUNNER_SANDBOX_MEMORY_MB=2048, RUNNER_MAX_SANDBOXES=4). These describe self-host only.

fleet.notes: Agent identities/integration calls/model credits, not documented per-agent managed VMs. Number of registered agents must not become default_max_instances. No hosted fleet quota established.

own_agent_api.quote: // POST /conversations — start a new exchange with a hosted agent.
own_agent_api.note: Harness = OneCLI's own hosted agent (bundled 'jcode' runtime behind the vendor-neutral @onecli/agent-protocol harness interface in the sandbox supervisor). Bearer-token REST routes: POST /conversations, GET /conversations?agentId=, GET /:id/events (transcript), GET /:id/stream (SSE live tail), POST /:id/turns, POST /:id/messages (follow-ups), POST /:turnId/abort. Documented UX is dashboard/Slack chat; these routes are not in the public API reference (source only). Claude Code/Codex/Cursor are not driven: 'onecli run -- claude' only wraps a local agent with gateway proxy settings.

egress_allowlist.quote: Each agent lives in its own sandbox, and the only way out is the gateway, which checks every request against your policy and injects the credentials granted to that agent.
egress_allowlist.note: Policy rules with network targets by hostPattern (plus app/connection/secret targets), first-match, each level ends in a Default Rule (Allow or Block) so default-deny is possible; org rules are a ceiling agents/projects cannot loosen; also per-app host blocklists. Self-host runner: sandboxes join an internal Docker network 'that network has NO route out', gateway dual-homed (runner README), so non-HTTP egress is simply blocked. IP/CIDR rules not documented. External agents via 'onecli run' only get proxy env vars (not enforced).

egress_http_rules.note: Host + path pattern + HTTP method, block/allow, per-agent rate limits (429), human approval holds, request-body conditions ('Conditions narrow a rule beyond its targets by inspecting the request body'), and per-tool rules for catalog apps. HTTPS inspected via MITM.

guest_firewall.note: OneCLI Cloud: 'One micro-VM per agent ... and root on that VM' (blog Why We Gave Every Agent a Computer), own kernel. Self-hosted Docker runner: sandboxes run with CapDrop ALL, no-new-privileges and default seccomp (runner README), so iptables/nftables would NOT work there.

secret_proxy.quote: If allowed, the gateway matches the target host and path against the credentials **granted to that agent**, decrypts the match, and injects it as a header (e.g. `Authorization: Bearer ...`) or query parameter.
secret_proxy.note: Core product: Rust MITM gateway; generic secrets for any host pattern (header or query-param injection, value templates), plus anthropic/openai types, OAuth app connections with token refresh (40+ apps), AWS SigV4 request signing, GitHub tokens into API calls and git-over-HTTPS (Basic auth), Bitwarden/1Password vault pull. Agents see placeholders ('onecli-managed' stubs). Non-HTTP (databases, SSH, raw git://) not covered; in sandboxes such traffic has no route out. Also usable standalone for external agents via 'onecli run' or SDK-injected Docker proxy config.
